_comment: Latency and error budgets for the endpoints a real user waits on. perf_digest.py
reads this, measures the last N hours of ACTUAL production traffic from Xano's request
history, and alerts only on a breach.
Raising a budget here is a decision to accept that experience — make it in a reviewed
commit, not to silence an alert. Budgets were set from the 2026-09-12 baseline (2,997
requests, 05:58-15:32 UTC): roughly 'a bit worse than a good day', so normal variance
is quiet and a real regression is not.
Three budgets start RED on purpose - ep119 p95, ep119 cache hit rate, and the global
race-401 rate. They encode the two known open problems so that fixing them is what
turns the check green, and so a fix cannot silently regress later.
_health_watch_comment: Endpoints that get the daily deep-dive (perf_digest.py --health): failure reasons, top queries, slow-time drivers, and a row per day in the HEALTH_TABLE_ID history table.

global._comment: Applied across all app traffic in the window.

119.name: wptp_updated_mappings_search
119.note: Discovery search. Highest-volume call a user waits on. Real users saw 45.7% cache hits on the 2026-09-12 baseline because task 8 was warming 23 keys that shared ZERO overlap with the 89 keys the app requests; it was realigned to 9 observed keys the same day.
119._cache_note: 55, not 60. Of 89 keys seen in a day, 80 were requested by exactly ONE visitor, and a key's first request is a miss by definition — so ~78 of 102 daily misses are unwarmable in principle and the ceiling from warming alone is about 58%. A 60% budget would be permanently unreachable, and a budget you cannot meet is one you learn to ignore. 55% sits above the realigned expectation and well above the 45.7% broken state, so it catches drift without crying wolf. Raising the ceiling itself means making the UNCACHED path faster, which is an ep119 change.

121.note: Map. Wide bounding boxes are the slow path.

216.note: Tier-aware access badge. 81% of calls 401'd on the 2026-09-12 baseline; 40 sessions never rendered it at all. The token-wait fix is built and waiting on a WeWeb publish.
